title: Blackbody radiation
source_status: User-provided topic sequence and dates; not independently verified

formulas.name: Planck–Einstein relation
formulas.when_to_use: To calculate the energy carried by a photon from its frequency.
assumptions: The electromagnetic excitation is treated as a photon.
common_mistakes: Mixing ordinary frequency ν with angular frequency ω.

formulas.name: Wien displacement law
formulas.when_to_use: To relate a blackbody's temperature to the wavelength where its spectrum peaks.
common_mistakes: Confusing the spectral peak with total emitted power

concepts.definition: Temperature times the peak wavelength of the per-wavelength blackbody spectrum; the per-frequency peak is different.
Ideal absorber and emitter of electromagnetic radiation; spectral distribution depends on temperature.
Classical Rayleigh–Jeans theory predicts unphysical divergence of radiation energy at high frequencies.
For light in vacuum frequency and wavelength satisfy ν=c/λ.
concepts.when_to_use: For electromagnetic waves in vacuum; in a medium use phase velocity.
concepts.source_status: User-supplied lecture slide; explanatory notation clarified

concepts.definition: Photon energy is inversely proportional to its vacuum wavelength.
concepts.when_to_use: Use λ in nm for the numerical approximation.
concepts.source_status: User-supplied lecture slide; explanatory notation clarified

concepts.definition: A photon has momentum despite zero invariant rest mass.
concepts.when_to_use: Use vacuum wavelength and photon energy.
concepts.source_status: User-supplied lecture slide; explanatory notation clarified

concepts.definition: Circularly polarized photon states have helicities ±ℏ along the propagation direction.
concepts.when_to_use: Helicity is the spin projection, not a classical spinning object.
concepts.source_status: User-supplied lecture slide; explanatory notation clarified

concepts.definition: Photons have zero invariant mass but nonzero energy and momentum.
concepts.when_to_use: Do not confuse invariant mass with E/c².
concepts.source_status: User-supplied lecture slide; explanatory notation clarified

concepts.definition: Angular wavenumber k differs from spectroscopic wavenumber ν̃.
concepts.when_to_use: k has units rad/m; ν̃ is often reported in cm⁻¹.
concepts.source_status: User-supplied lecture slide; explanatory notation clarified
